overview: RaR (Rubrics as Rewards) extends RLVR to non-verifiable domains by generating instance-specific, checklist-style rubrics from reference answers and using them as structured reward signals for on-policy GRPO reinforcement learning, evaluated on medical (HealthBench) and scientific (GPQA-Diamond) reasoning tasks.

modules.name: Instance-Specific Rubric Generation Module
modules.description: Generates per-prompt rubric criteria using a strong LLM conditioned on reference answers. Each rubric contains 7–20 self-contained items with categorical labels (Essential/Important/Optional/Pitfall) and numeric weights. Supports both medical and science domain prompt templates and enforces the four desiderata (expert grounding, comprehensive coverage, criterion importance, self-contained evaluation).

modules.name: Rubric Dataset Construction Module
modules.description: Constructs the RaR-Medicine and RaR-Science training datasets by aggregating prompts from multiple source corpora, pairing each prompt with its generated rubric and reference answer. Handles data deduplication, topic categorization, rubric statistics computation, and train/validation splitting.

modules.name: Explicit Reward Aggregation Module
modules.description: Implements explicit reward computation: each rubric criterion is independently evaluated by an LLM judge as a binary satisfaction check, then aggregated via a weighted normalized sum. Maps categorical weights (Essential=1.0, Important=0.7, Optional=0.3, Pitfall=0.9) to numeric values and normalizes across prompts with varying rubric counts.

modules.name: Implicit Reward Aggregation Module
modules.description: Implements implicit reward computation: all rubric criteria and their categorical weights are passed together to an LLM judge, which produces a single holistic Likert rating (1–10) that is then normalized to [0,1]. Delegates aggregation to the judge model itself, avoiding manual weight tuning.

modules.name: LLM-as-Judge Interface Module
modules.description: Provides a unified interface for calling LLM judge models (e.g., GPT-4o-mini, Qwen variants) to evaluate responses. Manages prompt templating for different evaluation modes (direct Likert, reference Likert, explicit rubric check, implicit rubric rating), JSON output parsing, rate limiting, and result caching.

modules.name: Policy Rollout and Response Sampling Module
modules.description: Samples multiple responses (k=16) from the current policy model for each training prompt using specified temperature and context length settings. Manages batched generation with the policy model, handles tokenization/detokenization, and collects rollout groups for GRPO advantage computation.

modules.name: GRPO Training Loop Module
modules.description: Implements the Group Relative Policy Optimization on-policy RL training loop. Computes group-based advantages from rubric rewards within each prompt's rollout group, applies policy gradient updates with clipping, manages the constant-with-warmup learning rate schedule, and handles gradient accumulation and checkpointing.

modules.name: HealthBench Rubric-Based Evaluation Module
modules.description: Evaluates trained models on HealthBench using physician-authored rubrics. Generates greedy-decoded responses, computes per-axis scores (accuracy, completeness, context awareness, instruction following, communication quality) and overall scores using the official HealthBench evaluation pipeline with GPT-4o-mini as judge.

modules.name: GPQA-Diamond Multiple-Choice Evaluation Module
modules.description: Evaluates trained models on GPQA-Diamond across multiple independent runs. Handles answer choice permutation to reduce positional bias, parses boxed answer formats with a GPT-4o verifier fallback, and reports mean accuracy with 95% confidence intervals over runs.

modules.name: Judge Alignment Evaluation Module
modules.description: Measures how well LLM judges of varying sizes align with human preferences. Uses paired preferred/rejected responses from HealthBench, computes pairwise preference accuracy under rubric-guided and rubric-free settings across judge scales, and quantifies the rubric benefit for smaller judges.

modules.name: Perturbed Response Generation Module
modules.description: Creates degraded versions of ideal HealthBench responses using structured perturbation strategies (medical accuracy, completeness, clarity, safety, specificity, structure, tone). Tracks added/removed chunks, filters for objective quality degradation while maintaining plausibility, and produces balanced preference pairs for alignment evaluation.

modules.name: Ablation Experiment Framework Module
modules.description: Orchestrates controlled ablation studies including: rubric design element ablation (essential-only, no categorical labels, no pitfall criteria), rubric generation strategy ablation (human vs. synthetic, with vs. without reference answers, different LLM generators), and policy model robustness ablation (7B vs. 3B base models). Manages experiment configuration and result collection.

modules.name: Baseline Reward Method Module
modules.description: Implements rubric-free baselines: Direct-Likert (single holistic 1–10 score normalized to [0,1]), Reference-Likert (score by comparison to reference answer), and RaR-Predefined (fixed generic rubric checklist with uniform weights applied to all prompts). Ensures fair comparison by sharing the same GRPO training loop and judge model.

modules.name: Experiment Configuration, Logging, and Reporting Module
modules.description: Manages YAML/JSON-based experiment configurations with inheritance, integrates training metrics logging with TensorBoard/Wandb, handles model checkpoint save/load, and aggregates final results into tables and figures (per-axis HealthBench bar charts, GPQA confidence interval plots, judge alignment curves across model scales).
